I shall receive it in monthly installments; installments, slender and long, and in any case you will be a valued patron from now on. No, no, you need not stand on ceremony in the least. paragraphs.source_en: Meitei said, “What on earth is that? Some moral verse? A moral verse without so much as common sense, is it not? In any case, he pays ten yen every month for five years, which means the other party need only make sixty payments and the account is settled. But this is precisely the dreadful thing about habit: after repeating the same act month after month for a full sixty times, at the sixty-first time he still feels inclined to pay, and at the sixty-second time he feels the same. The sixty-second, the sixty-third, and so on, one payment after another, until whenever the due date arrives, unless he pays those ten yen, he feels somehow unsatisfied. Human beings seem clever, but in fact they have a very great weakness: they are led astray by habit. By taking advantage of that weakness, I can pocket an unearned ten yen every month.”
